parameters.content:
## Job page API
Five endpoints behind the job page. **Nothing here calls Claude.** The three that change data (`generate`, `status`, `notes`) first check the `X-JobHunter: 1` header, so a web page on another site cannot trigger them. Ids are checked as UUIDs inside the SQL before use. Every answer is quick (well under 30 s).

- `POST api/jobs/generate` queues a run
- `GET api/jobs/detail` the job page data
- `POST api/jobs/status`, `POST api/jobs/notes`
- `GET api/jobs/download` Word or PDF

## Generate
Only **records** a request: one `pending` generation run. The Generate documents workflow picks it up on its schedule.
The insert is a single statement. The partial unique index (one active run per job) decides a double click or a second tab: `on conflict do nothing` returns no row, and the answer is `409 generation_in_progress`. Not ready: the job's details are not read yet (`422 job_not_ready`) or there is no analysed base CV (`422 base_cv_not_ready`). Nothing is queued then.

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner, [2] job id (text, checked as a UUID below)
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments. The parameters are
-- substituted everywhere in the text, comments included, which breaks the query.
-- One statement: the insert only happens when the job and the base CV are ready. A second active
-- run for the job violates the partial unique index; on conflict do nothing then returns no row.
with p as (select case when $2::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $2::text::uuid end as id),
j as (
  select jobs.id, jobs.extraction_status from jobs, p
  where jobs.id = p.id and jobs.owner_id = $1::uuid
), cv as (
  select 1 as one from base_documents
  where owner_id = $1::uuid and kind = 'cv' and active and analysis_status = 'done' and not source_removed
  limit 1
), ins as (
  insert into generation_runs (owner_id, job_id)
  select $1::uuid, j.id from j
  where j.extraction_status = 'done' and exists (select 1 from cv)
  on conflict do nothing
  returning id
)
select (select id from ins) as run_id,
       exists (select 1 from j) as job_found,
       coalesce((select extraction_status from j), '') as extraction_status,
       exists (select 1 from cv) as cv_ready;

parameters.content:
## Job page data
`GET api/jobs/detail?id=` answers the job, its latest generation run and its latest document version (with the cost of that run). A match score is shown only when it was worked out from the CV in use now, the same rule as the job list. The run's `error` is returned only when it is one of the Generate workflow's own messages; anything else (raw error text) becomes a fixed generic message.

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner, [2] job id (text, checked as a UUID below)
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments (see the generate query).
-- Same score rule as the job list: shown only when worked out from the CV in use now.
with p as (select case when $2::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $2::text::uuid end as id),
cur as (
  select content_hash from base_documents
  where owner_id = $1::uuid and kind = 'cv' and active and analysis_status = 'done' and not source_removed
  limit 1
), j as (
  select jobs.*,
    (jobs.match_basis_hash is not null
      and jobs.match_basis_hash = (select content_hash from cur)) as basis_ok
  from jobs, p
  where jobs.id = p.id and jobs.owner_id = $1::uuid
), g as (
  select r.* from generation_runs r, j where r.job_id = j.id
  order by r.created_at desc, r.id desc limit 1
), v as (
  select d.*, b.source_ref as base_cv_source_ref from document_versions d
  join j on d.job_id = j.id
  left join base_documents b on b.id = d.base_cv_id
  order by d.version_no desc limit 1
)
select
  exists (select 1 from j) as found,
  (select json_build_object(
    'id', j.id, 'title', j.title, 'employer', j.employer, 'advertiser', j.advertiser, 'url', j.url,
    'status', j.status, 'rawText', j.raw_text,
    'matchScore',       case when j.basis_ok then j.match_score end,
    'matchExplanation', case when j.basis_ok then j.match_explanation end,
    'matchBreakdown',   case when j.basis_ok then j.match_breakdown end,
    'warnings', j.warnings, 'companyNotes', j.company_notes) from j) as job,
  (select json_build_object(
    'status', g.status, 'stage', g.stage, 'round', g.round, 'attempts', g.attempts, 'error', g.error) from g) as generation,
  (select json_build_object(
    'id', v.id, 'versionNo', v.version_no, 'label', v.label,
    'createdAt', to_char(v.created_at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"'),
    'templateId', v.template_id, 'cv', v.cv, 'coverLetter', v.cover_letter, 'reasons', v.reasons,
    'keywordCoverage', v.keyword_coverage, 'review', v.review, 'checks', v.checks,
    'baseCvSourceRef', v.base_cv_source_ref,
    'costUsd', coalesce((select sum(c.cost_usd) from cost_log c where c.generation_run_id = v.run_id), 0)::float8
  ) from v) as version;

parameters.content:
## Change status
Any of the five statuses is allowed from the page. A history row is written only when the status really changes (the row is locked while it is compared, so two clicks cannot both record the same change). A bad status is `400 bad_status`.

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner, [2] job id (text, checked as a UUID below), [3] the new status (text)
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments (see the generate query).
with p as (select case when $2::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $2::text::uuid end as id),
cur as (
  select jobs.id, jobs.status from jobs, p
  where jobs.id = p.id and jobs.owner_id = $1::uuid
  for update of jobs
), upd as (
  update jobs set status = $3::text, updated_at = now()
  from cur
  where jobs.id = cur.id
    and $3::text in ('new', 'cv_ready', 'applied', 'interviewing', 'closed')
    and cur.status is distinct from $3::text
  returning jobs.id, cur.status as old_status
), hist as (
  insert into job_status_history (job_id, from_status, to_status)
  select id, old_status, $3::text from upd
  returning 1
)
select exists (select 1 from cur) as found,
       ($3::text in ('new', 'cv_ready', 'applied', 'interviewing', 'closed')) as valid;

parameters.content:
## Company notes
Free text, a string of at most 4000 characters. Anything else is `400 bad_notes` and nothing is saved.

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner, [2] job id (text, checked as a UUID below), [3] the notes (text), [4] whether the notes
-- are a string of at most 4000 characters
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments (see the generate query).
with p as (select case when $2::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $2::text::uuid end as id),
upd as (
  update jobs set company_notes = $3::text, updated_at = now()
  from p
  where jobs.id = p.id and jobs.owner_id = $1::uuid and $4::boolean
  returning jobs.id
)
select exists (select 1 from jobs, p where jobs.id = p.id and jobs.owner_id = $1::uuid) as found;

parameters.content:
## Download
`GET api/jobs/download?id=&doc=cv|cover_letter&format=docx|pdf` renders the latest stored version on demand through the worker (`/generation/render`); no file is kept. The answer is the file with `Content-Disposition: attachment`. File name: `{name} - CV - {target}` or `{name} - Cover letter - {target}`, target = employer, else advertiser, else Job; only letters, digits, space and `. _ ( ) -` are kept, at most 100 characters before the extension. No version: `404 no_version`. Bad parameters: `400 bad_request`.

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner, [2] job id (text, already checked as a UUID)
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments (see the generate query).
select exists (select 1 from jobs where id = $2::uuid and owner_id = $1::uuid) as found,
  (select row_to_json(t) from (
    select d.template_id as "templateId", d.cv, d.cover_letter as "coverLetter",
           j.employer, j.advertiser
    from document_versions d join jobs j on j.id = d.job_id
    where d.job_id = $2::uuid and j.owner_id = $1::uuid
    order by d.version_no desc limit 1
  ) t) as version;
